request.spec:
Rates can be pasted as lines of grade,rate,from,to (the last two may be absent or blank) into a
rate import box. Every line is checked first with the rate form's rules; if any fails, an error
shows and nothing is set; otherwise every line is set in order exactly as the form would set it
(replacing a rate for the same grade and from-date, writing RATE_SET). Show how many were set.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Rates can be pasted as lines of grade,rate,from,to (the last two may be absent or blank) into a
rate import box. Every line is checked first with the rate form's rules; if any fails, an error
shows and nothing is set; otherwise every line is set in order exactly as the form would set it
(replacing a rate for the same grade and from-date, writing RATE_SET). Show how many were set.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
I've added the rate import box. The main "import rates" test passes, but `bin/e2e` as a whole still fails: 2 of the 4 tests fail, for a reason that comes from the spec itself rather than from this change.

**Results:**
- "import rates" passes. That covers the counts shown (3 and 2), all four refusals (grade `D`, rate `1.005`, a to-date before the from-date, an empty paste), replacing an existing rate, blank lines being skipped, and the exact audit lines.
- "scenario 3" passes.
- "scenario 1" and "scenario 2" fail on the spec's own lines 195 and 550. Both expect `sheet-parent` to show the literal text `"__SHEET__-p"`. The app correctly shows the real parent id (e.g. `smvk2lcsyrmxm-p`). It looks like a placeholder in the spec that was never replaced with the sheet id; line 635 has the same placeholder. I can't edit the spec, and making the app print `__SHEET__-p` would be wrong, so I left these two failing. The fix is in the spec: use `` `${sheet}-p` `` there.

**What I changed:**
- **New endpoint** `POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/import-rates` (`src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/api/sheets/{sheetId}/import-rates.POST.yml`):
  - `ValidateRateImport` reads each non-blank line as grade,rate,from,to and checks it with the rate form's rules. If any line fails, the error names that line and nothing is written to the store or the audit file.
  - `ImportRates` then sets each rate in order, exactly as the form does. For each line it saves the rate (replacing one with the same grade and from-date), writes `RATE_SET`, and then any `ROLLUP`/`TOTALS` lines. It responds with how many were set.
- **Shared rules:** the form's checks and the `RATE_SET` line now live in a new class, `RateRules`. `ValidateRate` and `AuditRateSet` call it, so the import and the form can't drift apart. I had to move them out because OfficeFloor won't start if a step class has more than one public method, even a static one.
- **Front end:** a new box in `src/main/frontend/features/rates/import.slot.tsx`, placed just after the rates panel. It has the test ids `import-rates`, `import-rates-submit`, `import-rates-set` and `import-rates-error`. The error clears when you edit the text or submit again.
